title: Framework/PBC compact-support and open-exchange comparison
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between quasi-separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$ be a quasi-compact open immersion, and put $X_V=X\times_YV$, with projections $u:X_V\hookrightarrow X$ and $f_V:X_V\to V$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-open-immersion]. Supply a compactification $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow T,p:T\to Y)$, with $j$ quasi-compact open and $p$ proper, and its pullback $c_V$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. No separatedness of any of these schemes over $k$ is assumed. Every scheme just named is required to be Noetherian, meaning quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and to have finite Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].

For each finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Omega$, write $R=\mathcal O_E$, choose a uniformizer $\varpi$, and put $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. At the integral stage let $\mathcal C_T$ be the framework derived-complete constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and $\mathcal P_T$ the PBC bounded constructible complete category [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. Let $J_T:\mathcal C_T\simeq\mathcal P_T$ be the coefficient-presentation equivalence inverse to $\Phi_{E,T}$ of [def-pur-completed-coefficient-presentation-transport], restricted to these full categories. At $E$ and $\Omega$ use exactly its raw rationalized and common-stage equivalences of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison]. In the formulas below $J$ and the operations are taken at any one of these three stages.

Write $F_h^{\mathrm{sf}}$ for the framework compact-support functor of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], whose integral value is
$$F_f^{\mathrm{sf}}K=R\!\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n Rp_{*,A_n}j_!(K\otimes_R^LA_n),$$
using its specified strict quotient transitions, and write $F_h^{\mathrm{pbc}}=Rp_*j_!$ for the completed PBC functor [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification], with raw rationalization and common-stage passage at field coefficients. Here $h=f,f_V$. Write $P_a^{\mathrm{sf}}$ and $P_a^{\mathrm{pbc}}$ for the completed pullbacks along $a=u,v$, respectively [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and their field forms.

There are specified natural isomorphisms
$$b_h:J_{\operatorname{target}(h)}F_h^{\mathrm{sf}}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_h^{\mathrm{pbc}}J_{\operatorname{source}(h)},\qquad a_s:J_{\operatorname{source}(s)}P_s^{\mathrm{sf}}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_s^{\mathrm{pbc}}J_{\operatorname{target}(s)}\quad(s=u,v).$$
Their integral normalization is the identity of the whole strict reduction diagrams, followed by the canonical proper-direct-image/derived-limit and completed-open-extension/derived-limit comparisons. At field coefficients they are the scalar-localized and common-stage images with the specified coefficient associators.

Let $\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{sf}}:P_v^{\mathrm{sf}}F_f^{\mathrm{sf}}\to F_{f_V}^{\mathrm{sf}}P_u^{\mathrm{sf}}$ be the framework exchange formed on that same strict quotient diagram: first the proper adjunction mate, then the open adjunction comparison, followed by total derived inverse limit and the canonical endpoint identifications. Let $\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{pbc}}$ be precisely the ordered completed exchange [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map], and its specified rationalized/common-stage forms. For every input $K\in\mathcal C_X$, put
$$S_K=P_v^{\mathrm{pbc}}(b_{f,K})\circ a_{v,F_f^{\mathrm{sf}}K},\qquad T_K=F_{f_V}^{\mathrm{pbc}}(a_{u,K})\circ b_{f_V,P_u^{\mathrm{sf}}K}.$$
Then the equality of actual natural transformations is
$$\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{pbc}}_{J_XK}\circ S_K=T_K\circ J_V(\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{sf}}_K).$$
These identifications are natural for isomorphisms of the entire compactification/open-square diagram, including semilinear field automorphisms, respect identity and iterated open restriction, and commute with finite coefficient-field extension and its associators. If the diagram is defined over $k_0$, they identify the induced geometric-Frobenius Weil structures [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. The assertion compares the specified functors and arrows; it does not assert base-change invertibility.

source.place: Common-stage descent of the compact-support exchange; auxiliary comparison of the framework reduction-tower construction with the completed PBC construction, made explicit for open target restriction

proof.text: Work first over $R=\mathcal O_E$. Its discrete valuation ring property and the finite perfect quotients $A_n$ are [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr, lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect]; thus the adic datum is applicable. By [def-pur-completed-coefficient-presentation-transport], $J_W$ is restriction along the specified completed ring isomorphism, retaining all finite projections. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], it restricts to precisely the two full constructible categories in the statement. Its hypotheses hold at every corner and at $T,T_V$: Noetherian and finite-dimensional are explicit assumptions, and $\ell$ is a unit since these are $k$-schemes. In particular $J_XK$ has compatible bounded-below etale-origin witnesses, by the definition [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. This does not impose a uniform finite-Tor bound on the $A_n$-complexes.

source.place: Agent supplement: fix the integral presentation before common-stage descent

proof.text: Make all identifications on whole strict diagrams. In either presentation choose one flat-term K-flat representative $Q$ and the simultaneous quotients $Q\otimes_R A_n$, with transition $1\otimes(A_{n+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_n)$. The specified coefficient isomorphism sends each quotient projection to the same projection. On a scheme edge the two coefficient structure maps agree: their composites with every finite projection send a constant coefficient to that same coefficient, so the universal property of the inverse limit identifies the maps. The scheme-edge coefficient maps are isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Restriction along a ring isomorphism is exact, preserves products and K-injectives, and is identity on underlying sections with their transported action. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction] with these ring isomorphisms and indexing category $\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{op}$. It compares direct images and inverse images as diagram functors and preserves their adjuncts. On open extension the same assertion follows directly from the sheafified extension presheaf: changing the scalar action changes neither its sections nor its unit and counit. Thus these are comparisons of diagram operations and adjunctions, including transitions, rather than comparisons chosen after evaluation.

source.place: Agent supplement: coefficient-presentation transport on strict diagrams

proof.text: For a quasi-compact open $j:X\hookrightarrow T$, let $M=j_!J_XK$. The completed-open theorem [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison] says that $M$ is complete. Its strict reduction diagram is canonically $j_!(J_XK)_\bullet$. To see the normalization, the module tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] gives the map on flat representatives; $j_!$ preserves K-flatness because its tensor with an acyclic complex is $j_!$ of the tensor with its exact restriction. At every transition the tensor map sends a section tensored with $a$ to the same section tensored with the quotient of $a$; therefore it is a map of quotient diagrams. By [prop-weil-pbc-koszul-reconstruction], the canonical quotient completion map consequently gives $\rho_{j,K}:j_!J_XK\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim j_!(J_XK)_\bullet$. Use the specified strict-limit comparison, not a choice of a triangle: [lem-sf-strict-roos-derived-limit-comparison] identifies the framework cone with total derived limit, naturally and with the same projections. Its product-exactness hypothesis is [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. The construction also applies to $j_V$. For later composition coherence, $j_!$ also preserves products: choose a closed complement $i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme]. The exact open/closed sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], applied to $j_*F$, identifies $j_!F$ with $\ker(j_*F\to i_*i^{-1}j_*F)$. Right adjoints $j_*,i_*$ preserve products; $i^{-1}$ does so by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation], with coefficients $i^{-1}R_T$. Products preserve kernels, giving the required product comparison. This proves the module version of Stacks 09BP and supplies the hypothesis used in Step 9.

source.place: Tag 09BP, lemma-j-shriek-limits; completed-open reconstruction with the canonical quotient maps

proof.text: Let $c_p:Rp_*R\lim N_\bullet\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim Rp_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}N_\bullet$ be exactly [prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]. Set $b_f=Rp_*(\rho_{j,K}^{-1})\circ c_p^{-1}$ after the diagram identifications of Step 2 and the framework definition [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Step 2 only handles ring isomorphisms; the framework levels $\operatorname{Res}_nRp_{*,A_n}j_!K_n$ are identified with the evaluations of $Rp_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ on the restricted tower $j_!(J_XK)_\bullet$ by [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison]: its comparison $F_RV_{X,n}\cong V_{Y,n}F_n$ is a comparison of derived strict-diagram functors, compatible with restriction along $A_m\to A_n$, so it carries the quotient transitions. This has source $J_YF_f^{\mathrm{sf}}K$ and target $Rp_*j_!J_XK$. The transition in the framework definition is the image of the actual quotient transition under this same composite: its scalar-restriction comparison is the canonical one of [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars], coherent for successive quotients. Thus the entire diagram, not merely the list of values, is the one used in $c_p$. Define $b_{f_V}$ in the same way. Naturality follows from that of $\rho$ and $c_p$. Both sides restrict to the claimed constructible categories, since [lem-cbc-integral-compact-support-uniform-restriction] applies to $f$ and $f_V$, and Step 1 identifies these categories.

For $s=u,v$, the framework construction [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the PBC construction [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] apply the same finite module pullbacks to the simultaneous quotient diagram. Under Step 2 the coefficient maps have the same components. Apply [lem-cbc-adic-pullback-presentation-transport]: its identity on balanced tensors gives a derived strict-diagram isomorphism, and its total-limit image defines $a_s$. That lemma also identifies the quotient augmentation and its completion unit, so this is precisely the stipulated normalization. Use the natural Roos/total-limit identification of Step 3 on the framework side. These are isomorphisms of completed pullback functors. For their identity/composition and scalar comparisons use [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], whose comparisons are defined using the counit of the whole quotient diagram and are associative and unital. This result is stated for arbitrary scheme morphisms and has no absolute separatedness or finite-Tor restriction.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (5); completed pullback on the strict reduction diagram

proof.text:
Write $w:T_V\hookrightarrow T$. In the constant-$R$ strict-tower model put $N_\bullet=\operatorname{Res}(J_XK)_\bullet$, and denote termwise open extension by $J_j$, inverse image by $G$, and derived diagram direct image by $R_p^{\mathcal T}$. The ordered diagram map is
$$e_\bullet=(R_{p_V}^{\mathcal T}\beta_{j,w})\circ E_p^{\mathcal T}:G_vR_p^{\mathcal T}J_jN_\bullet\longrightarrow R_{p_V}^{\mathcal T}J_{j_V}G_uN_\bullet.$$
Here $E_p^{\mathcal T}$ is the mate of the pullback square and $\beta$ is the open unit-mate, with the normalizations of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. The framework exchange in the question is exactly the realization of this map: its defining order is proper mate, then open comparison. Step 2 preserves the units and counits forming those mates. Passing from the finite $A_n$-level systems to constant-$R$ towers is restriction along the non-flat $R\to A_n$. Derived direct image commutes with it on whole diagrams by [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison]. Applied on the diagram sites with $R_X=((A_n)_X)_n$, [lem-pur-ringed-coefficient-restriction-counit] carries the finite counits to the constant ones. The units follow by the triangle identities, both comparisons being isomorphisms. Inverse image and $j_!$ act on underlying sheaves. The finite open comparisons commute with quotient transitions as actual complex maps by [lem-cbc-finite-open-exchange-scalars]; hence this identifies the diagram arrow itself. The proper factor is likewise the normalized whole-diagram mate, not a lift characterized by its evaluated arrows.

source.place: Ordered proper and open factors; identify their strict-diagram lifts

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-complete-proetale-strict-tower-realization] to $J_XK$, $c$ and its base change by $v$. The hypotheses are now verified: $p$ is proper, $j$ is quasi-compact, $J_XK$ is complete with compatible etale-origin witnesses (Step 1), $j_!J_XK$ is complete and has strict quotient tower $j_!(J_XK)_\bullet$ (Step 3). That lemma identifies precisely the ordered completed exchange [def-cbc-completed-exchange-map] with $R\lim(e_\bullet)$ under its stated coefficient, reduction, direct-image/limit and extension/limit identifications. Its proper normalization uses $H'\mathcal R(e)H^{-1}$ in the derived diagram category; thus it applies to the particular PBC arrow in the question. The framework arrow of Step 6 and this PBC arrow are images of the same actual diagram map under the endpoint identifications already fixed in Steps 3–5. No base-change invertibility theorem is used.

source.place: First sentence: the two ordered factors, using the strict-tower realization rather than finite evaluations

proof.text:
Here is the endpoint calculation. Let $A_\bullet,B_\bullet$ be the source and target diagrams of $e_\bullet$. Write $d_s:J_VP_v^{\mathrm{sf}}F_f^{\mathrm{sf}}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim A_\bullet$ and $d_t:J_VF_{f_V}^{\mathrm{sf}}P_u^{\mathrm{sf}}\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim B_\bullet$ for the framework identifications, and $q_s:P_v^{\mathrm{pbc}}F_f^{\mathrm{pbc}}J_X\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim A_\bullet$, $q_t:F_{f_V}^{\mathrm{pbc}}P_u^{\mathrm{pbc}}J_X\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim B_\bullet$ for the PBC identifications. By the definitions in Steps 4–5, with $c_C\kappa_C=\operatorname{comp}_C$ ensuring the same quotient units, $q_sS=d_s$ and $q_tT=d_t$. Steps 6–7 say $J_V(\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{sf}})=d_t^{-1}R\lim(e_\bullet)d_s$ and $\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{pbc}}J_X=q_t^{-1}R\lim(e_\bullet)q_s$. Consequently
$$\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{pbc}}J_X\,S=q_t^{-1}R\lim(e_\bullet)d_s=T\,J_V(\operatorname{Ex}^{\mathrm{sf}}).$$
All identifications are natural, so this componentwise calculation is the required equality of natural transformations.

source.place: Agent supplement: conjugation calculation for the specified endpoints

proof.text: For identities and two successive open restrictions, use the pullback composition comparison of Step 5. The proper diagram mate respects composition by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](1),(2),(4), and the open diagram comparison respects identity and composition by [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. Thus the ordered diagram maps for two restrictions paste to the ordered map for their composite. The endpoint comparisons have the same property: on K-injective towers the proper/limit comparison is the underived equality $p_*\lim=\lim p_*$, and on the Roos model the open comparison applies the canonical product comparison to both summands. For composable functors $F,G$, their product comparisons satisfy $\phi_{FG}=\phi_F\circ F(\phi_G)$ because their composites with each product projection agree. Therefore these endpoint maps also compose. This is the specified comparison of [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit], not an arbitrary cone map. Applying the functorial total limit [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] proves identity and iterated-restriction coherence. An isomorphism of the entire diagram acts on the same sections, quotient maps and adjunctions, so the construction commutes with it; none of this uses $k$-linearity of the isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0A07, diagram-site proof; identity and composition of the canonical limit comparisons

proof.text: Check coefficient extension before passing to common stages. For $E\subset L$, [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] identifies the ordinary completed-coefficient scalar tensor with the framework strict-tower scalar construction by the specified completion map $\chi$. For proper direct image and completed pullback, use the comparisons and the exchange compatibility of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. For open extension use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor]: tensoring by the finite-free completed $\mathcal O_L$ coefficient commutes with $j_!$, already on module sheaves; its derived comparison is the same termwise map, since this scalar tensor is exact. It preserves the open unit and counit: after restriction to the open its map is multiplication of coefficients, while on the complementary extension summands both maps are zero. Thus it carries the open unit-mate to the open unit-mate. The presentation comparison uses the balanced-tensor normalization of [def-pur-completed-coefficient-presentation-transport]. Accordingly the two scalar images of each factor of $b,a,e_\bullet$ agree, including the completion unit; the proper-mate compatibility is the one explicitly asserted in the scalar-extension theorem. For three fields both routes act on pure tensors by $c\otimes(b\otimes x)\mapsto cb\otimes x$. The coefficient associators and their cocycle are those of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison], and the pullback completion comparisons obey precisely these associators by Step 5. This proves the asserted scalar compatibility without using a theorem limited to absolutely separated schemes or finite-Tor inputs.

source.place: Scalar extension through proper direct image and open extension, before common-stage descent

proof.text: At $E$ take the raw scalar localizations of all the integral functors, comparisons and equations. This is exactly the equivalence prescribed by [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison] and the field construction of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Each isomorphism retains its localized inverse. The integral naturality equation is $R$-linear, so after tensoring Hom groups with $E$ it is natural for every localized arrow; sums follow by additivity. Applying the localization functor to the equation of Step 8 proves it at $E$, and applying it to Steps 9–10 preserves their composition and coefficient equations.

source.place: Raw rationalization of the specified integral arrows

proof.text: At $\Omega$, represent an object by $(E,K)$ and an arrow over a common finite extension $L$. Define $a,b$ by their $L$-components, conjugated by the coefficient maps $j_{W,L/E}$ of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison]. Step 10 says that further extension to $L'$ gives the same representatives, with the stipulated associators, so these are well-defined maps in the Hom colimits. Their inverse representatives descend likewise. Naturality and the equation of Step 8 hold over $L$ by Step 11 and hence in the colimit. Every identity, pasting or scalar-associator equation involves finitely many representatives; put them over one common finite field and apply Steps 9–11. The intermediate comparison and its inverse cancel. This proves precisely the common-stage assertions, without changing either category by a Karoubi completion.

source.place: Common-stage descent of functors and exchange transformations

proof.text:
Finally suppose the diagram descends to $k_0$. Its geometric-Frobenius automorphisms form an isomorphism of the entire compactification/open diagram. The naturality established in Step 9 therefore intertwines the Frobenius exchange comparisons on the two presentations; Steps 11–12 give the same assertion at field coefficients. The equivalence's pullback comparison for scheme isomorphisms is exactly that of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison], normalized by the same quotient diagram as $a$. For a Weil pair $(K,\theta)$, its induced compact-support Weil arrow is the Frobenius exchange followed by $F_f(\theta)$. Naturality of $b_f$ for $\theta$, composed with the preceding intertwining square, gives
$$b_{f,K}\,J_Y(\theta_{F_f^{\mathrm{sf}}K})=\theta_{F_f^{\mathrm{pbc}}J_XK}\,P_{g_Y}^{\mathrm{pbc}}(b_{f,K})$$
with the specified comparison $J_YP_{g_Y}^{\mathrm{sf}}\cong P_{g_Y}^{\mathrm{pbc}}J_Y$ inserted on the source. This is exactly the intertwining condition of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. The identical argument for $a$ and the exchange equation identifies the induced Weil structures throughout. Scheme isomorphisms, not absolute separatedness over $k$, are what this argument uses.
